positions.title: Undergraduate Research Scientist
positions.description:
Advisors: Alexander Gimelbrant, Ph.D. and Clara Pereira, Ph.D.
Harvard–MIT Health Sciences and Technology (HST) Summer Research Program in Biomedical Informatics

❖ Designed and developed four applications in R and JavaScript to aid in experimental design, data collection, and visualization of drug screening data while in constant communication with wet lab.
❖ Streamlined ScreenSeq, a data analysis pipeline involving basic bioinformatics tools like Bowtie, Samtools, IGV, and homebrewed tools written in Perl, Python, and R.
❖ Gave a presentation of findings to a panel of Harvard Bioinformatics faculty and peers at the end of the program.

positions.title: Columbia University iGEM Team
positions.description:
Advisor: Harris Wang, Ph.D.

❖ Led the biological systems modeling division of the ColumbiaNYC team that won Silver Medal at the international iGEM (International Genetically Engineered Machines) competition.
❖ Project involved engineering bacteria that would utilize RNA interference (RNAi) as a potential cancer therapeutic via pathogenic invasion techniques.
❖ Honed wet lab techniques such as Bacterial Transformations, Cloning, Minipreps, Sequencing, and Lipofectamine assays.

positions.title: Research Intern
positions.description:
Advisor: Gang Fang, Ph.D.

❖ Led computational heavy and visualization projects that reconciled several DNA sequencing technologies. 
❖ Developed software for epigenetics projects in R, MATLAB, Python, and Scala, using Mt. Sinai's Minerva server for resource intensive runs.
❖ Collaborated with mentor and peers on different projects in the epigenetics department.

projects.title: Knowledge Trumps All — 2018 Columbia Data Science Society Hackathon
projects.description: "Knowledge Trumps All" was a project hacked together in less than 18 hours at the 2018 Columbia Data Science Society Hackathon. It won the Best Use of Google Cloud Platform prize. Our project involved using the Google Cloud Platform to perform NLP sentiment analysis on a variety of news articles, with the ultimate goal of determining the differences in writing style between news publishers. Additionally, we created a random forest model that was able to identify whether or not an inputted article would be promoted by the west wing. Finally, we created a website to display our analysis and allow users to use our model with their own choice of news articles.

projects.title: WaitER — PennApps XVIII Hackathon
projects.description: One of the biggest causes of crowding and wait times in emergency departments is “boarding,” a term for holding an admitted patient in the ER for hours or even days until an inpatient bed becomes available. Long wait times can affect patient outcomes in various ways: patients may get tired of waiting and leave without receiving medical treatment, especially when resources of the emergency department are overwhelmed. In order to alleviate some of the anxiety and stress associated with the process, we created WaitER, a web application that aims to bring transparency to patient wait times in the emergency room. WaitER provides a two-way channel for nurses and patients to communicate in real time.
